RentSplit Guide is a free educational resource for people sharing homes, bills, and the occasional dinner receipt.

What you’ll find here

Our original guides explain common ways to allocate rent and shared expenses, with formulas, assumptions, and worked examples. The calculator divides monthly rent equally between roommates using just two fields. The resource library collects 17 reading links and 6 Rent Split Calculator profiles on external websites.

The aim is to help you understand the choices and agree on a method. A mathematical result is a starting point for a conversation; it does not decide what every household should consider fair.

How the examples work

The calculator displays dollar amounts with two decimal places. Enter the monthly rent and number of roommates to see an equal share per person.

When rent cannot divide evenly into cents, a short rounding note shows how to cover the difference. For unequal bedrooms, follow the room-size guide and its worked example.

Your privacy

The calculator runs entirely in your browser. This site does not send your calculator inputs to a server, save them in local storage, or use analytics, advertising cookies, or accounts. Your numbers reset when the page reloads.

GitHub Pages or another hosting provider receives ordinary requests when you visit, including connection information such as an IP address. External websites linked from the resource library have their own privacy practices. A Search Console verification tag, if configured by the site owner, does not add visitor analytics.

Using the guidance

This site provides general education, not individualized legal, tax, or financial advice. Your lease, local requirements, and household agreement may affect what you owe. Restaurant taxes and service-charge practices also vary. Verify actual bills and agreements before paying.

External links are a reading collection, not an endorsement of a publisher or a claim that its content has been reviewed. All internal guides remain available without JavaScript.
